newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB faces digital TV profit challenge.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB faces digital TV profit challenge.

text.p: British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc Plc chief executive Sam Chisholm said on Friday that maintaining profit levels while launching digital television would be a "spectacular" achievement.

"It's hard to say what rate of profit increase you will show," Chisholm told a news conference, adding it would be a "spectacular" achievement to maintain profits through the digital launch and its associated costs.
He said BSkyB would be "defying the laws of gravity" if it could do everything it had to tackle in the current year and maintain profits at current levels.
BSkyB is gearing up for the launch of 200 channel digital satellite television in the spring of next year.
Looking at the company's digital TV plans, Chisholm said: "At this company we do sit back, think it through and get it right...We think we've got it right."

Chisholm, who is stepping down at the end of the year on health grounds, said pay television operator BSkyB's success came from supplying 25 percent of UK households. He said his successor Mark Booth would seek to target the 75 percent of homes that don't take BSkyB services.
"Our intention is to keep this company in rapid growth. We are going to be the company that leads the way," he said.

Chisholm said "50 percent (of households) is where you get to in this business", adding that was a prospect that would have the heads of terrestrial rivals such as ITV and Channel 4 and even the BBC waking up in the middle of the night.
